examples.ko: 그는 화가 나서 부모님께 극언을 했어요.
examples.en: He got angry and said harsh things to his parents.
There are many comments full of harsh words on the internet.

examples.ko: 아무리 화가 나도 극언은 삼가는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: No matter how angry you are, it is better to avoid extreme words.
The controversy grew because of the politician's harsh remarks.

examples.ko: 친구에게 극언을 듣고 한참 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: I heard harsh words from a friend and felt hurt for a long time.
Once you say really harsh things, it gets hard to make up.

explain: '막말'이나 '독설'과 비슷하지만 '극언'은 주로 글이나 뉴스에서 써요. '극언을 하다/삼가다/퍼붓다'처럼 함께 쓰는 말이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '심한 말'이라고 해도 충분해요.

phrases.en: Even when you are angry, don't say harsh things.
phrases.nuance_ko: '극언'과 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요. 아주 심한 말을 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 극언, meaning to say very harsh words.

phrases.en: You should refrain from harsh remarks during a debate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심한 말을 하지 않도록 조심하라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say one should be careful not to use harsh words.

phrases.en: I said something harsh to my friend, so I apologized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '극언' 대신 '심한 말'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, people say 심한 말 instead of 극언.

explain_en: It is close to '막말' (rude talk) or '독설' (venom), but '극언' is mostly seen in writing and news. It pairs with verbs like '하다', '삼가다' and '퍼붓다'. In everyday talk, '심한 말' is enough.

examples.en: The things you were worried about were all needless fears.
That kind of worry is nothing but groundless anxiety.

examples.ko: 합격할 수 있을지 걱정했는데 기우로 끝났어요.
examples.en: I worried about whether I'd pass, but it turned out to be needless.

examples.ko: 혹시 늦을까 봐 걱정했는데 쓸데없는 기우였네요.
examples.en: I was afraid we'd be late, but that was a pointless worry.

examples.ko: 그건 기우일 뿐이니까 너무 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.en: That's just an unfounded worry, so don't worry too much.

examples.ko: 사람들의 기우와 달리 행사는 무사히 끝났어요.
examples.en: Unlike what people feared, the event ended without a hitch.

explain: '기우였다', '기우에 불과하다'처럼 걱정한 일이 일어나지 않았거나 걱정이 필요 없었다는 걸 알았을 때 주로 써요. '기우제'는 비가 오기를 비는 제사로, 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 시험에 떨어질 거라는 걱정은 기우에 불과했어요.
phrases.en: The worry that I would fail the test turned out to be nothing more than needless worry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정할 만한 일이 아니었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that the worry was not worth worrying about.
phrases.en_equiv: to be nothing but needless worry

phrases.example: 시험이 어려울까 봐 한 걱정은 기우로 끝났어요.
phrases.en: My worry that the test would be hard ended up being unfounded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이 필요 없었다는 결과를 알게 됐을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you find out the worry was unnecessary after all.
phrases.en_equiv: to end up as groundless worry

phrases.en: I was worried it would rain, but it was needless worry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정하던 일이 일어나지 않아서 걱정할 필요가 없었다는 걸 알았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the feared thing did not happen and you realize the worry was unnecessary.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '기우였다' or '기우에 불과하다' when you find out that a feared thing didn't happen or the worry wasn't needed. '기우제' is a ritual to pray for rain, a different word.

examples.en: That story is complete nonsense.
Let me give you a fun nonsense quiz.
I think a rule like this is nonsense.

examples.ko: 친구가 낸 난센스 문제에 다 같이 웃었어요.
examples.en: We all laughed at the riddle my friend posed.

examples.ko: 어른들도 난센스 같은 일에 휘둘릴 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Even adults sometimes get pushed around by absurd things.
Nonsense comedies are funny because the plots are so wacky.

explain: '말도 안 되는 일'이라고 비판할 때도 쓰고, 엉뚱한 말장난을 하는 '난센스 퀴즈'로도 많이 써요. '넌센스'가 아니라 '난센스'로 써요.

phrases.en: My friend asked a funny nonsense quiz.
phrases.nuance_ko: 엉뚱한 답이 나오는 말장난 문제를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A wordplay riddle with a silly answer.

phrases.en: That's a nonsensical story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞뒤가 맞지 않는 말을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize something that makes no sense.

phrases.en: That claim is complete nonsense.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완전히'를 붙여 강하게 반박하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 완전히 makes it a strong rebuttal.

explain_en: It can criticize something as absurd, and it is also used for silly wordplay riddles called '난센스 퀴즈'. The standard spelling is '난센스', not '넌센스'.

en: to smile cynically; to smile sarcastically

examples.ko: 그는 내 말을 듣고 조용히 냉소했어요.
examples.en: He smiled coldly and quietly when he heard me.
People are cynical about politicians' promises.
I was upset because my friend scoffed at my plan.

examples.ko: 세상을 냉소하는 태도는 좋아 보이지 않아요.
examples.en: A cynical attitude toward the world doesn't look good.
Why does she talk in such a sneering way?

examples.ko: 처음에는 냉소하던 사람들도 결과를 보고 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Even people who were cynical at first were surprised by the result.

explain: '비웃다'와 비슷하지만 냉소하다는 차갑고 조용하게, 무시하는 마음으로 웃는 느낌이에요. 사람 말이나 계획, 세상 같은 것을 대상으로 '~을 냉소하다'라고 써요.

phrases.en: My friends laughed at my dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: '냉소하다'보다 일상에서 더 자주 쓰고 소리 내어 웃는 경우에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily speech than 냉소하다, and can include laughing out loud.

phrases.en: He spoke with a cold, sarcastic smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차갑게 웃으면서 말하는 모습을 연결형으로 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The connective form for speaking while smiling coldly.
phrases.en_equiv: to speak with a cynical smile

phrases.en: Please don't sneer at other people's efforts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 일을 무시하며 웃지 말라고 부탁하거나 경고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask or warn someone not to belittle others.

explain_en: It is close to '비웃다' (to laugh at), but 냉소하다 has a cold, quiet, dismissive feel. It takes an object, as in '~을 냉소하다', for things like someone's words, plans or the world.

examples.en: That reporter critiques movies sharply.

examples.ko: 친구의 그림을 비평해 달라는 부탁을 받았어요.
examples.en: I was asked to give feedback on my friend's painting.

examples.ko: 남의 작품을 비평하기는 쉬워도 만들기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It is easy to critique others' work but hard to make your own.
A critic reviewed the new novel.

examples.ko: 비평하는 글을 쓸 때는 근거가 필요해요.
examples.en: When writing a critical piece, you need evidence.
They criticized the policy and also offered an alternative.

explain: 비평하다는 책, 영화, 그림 같은 작품이나 정책의 좋은 점과 나쁜 점을 따져서 평가하는 일이에요. 단순히 나쁘게 말하는 '비난하다'와 달리 이유를 들어 분석한다는 느낌이에요. '평가하다'보다 글이나 말로 의견을 내놓는 쪽에 가까워요.

phrases.en: The reporter criticized the new policy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 어떤 일에 의견을 냈다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, used to say someone gave a critical opinion on something.

phrases.en: I read a piece reviewing a movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품을 평가하는 글을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for writing that evaluates a work.

phrases.example: 저는 제 글에 대해 선생님께 비평을 받았어요.
phrases.en: I received my teacher's critique of my writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내 작품에 대한 평가를 들었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your own work gets evaluated.

explain_en: Bipyeonghada means to judge the good and bad points of a work, such as a book, film, or policy, giving reasons. Unlike 비난하다, which is plain blame, it implies analysis. Compared with 평가하다, it leans toward stating an opinion in writing or speech.

t90.ax: A critic reviewed the new novel.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 소설에는 염세주의가 짙게 깔려 있어요.
examples.en: Pessimism runs thick through that author's novels.

examples.ko: 염세주의로 흐르지 않도록 좋은 사람들을 만나요.
examples.en: I meet good people so that I don't drift into pessimism.
I gave a presentation on pessimism in philosophy class.
Pessimism is the opposite way of thinking from optimism.
He talks like a pessimist, but he is actually kind.
This song expresses pessimism through humor.

explain: 철학이나 문학 이야기에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서는 '염세적이다'나 '비관적이다'처럼 풀어서 말해요. 반대말은 '낙관주의'예요.

phrases.en: After hardships kept coming, I fell into pessimism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상을 어둡게 보는 생각에 깊이 잠길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone sinks deep into a gloomy view of the world.

phrases.en: He calls himself a pessimist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 생각을 가진 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who holds that outlook.

phrases.en: This poem was written from a pessimistic point of view.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문학이나 철학 이야기에서 작품의 관점을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in literature or philosophy to describe a work's viewpoint.

explain_en: It is a stiff word for philosophy and literature talk. In daily life people say things like '염세적이다' or '비관적이다' instead. The opposite is '낙관주의'.

t90.ax: This song expresses pessimism through humor.

en: to be extreme; to be excessive

examples.en: How bad must it have been for that person to quit the company?
How bad must it have been that I couldn't even tell Mom?
How desperate must that child have been to tell a lie?
Do you think I would ask like this if it weren't so serious?
It must have been serious for a friend to come all the way to my house.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에서 일하는 사람은 오죽하겠어요.
examples.en: Imagine how hard it is for people who work outside on a cold day.

explain: '오죽하면 ~겠어요?', '오죽했으면 ~을까요?', '오죽하겠어요?'처럼 물음 꼴로 써요. '얼마나 힘들었으면 그랬겠어요'라는 공감의 말이에요. 대답을 바라는 질문이 아니고, 그 사람의 행동이나 처지를 이해해 줄 때 써요.

phrases.en: How hard it must be for a mother raising a child alone!
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧게 끝내는 말로, 그 사람의 힘든 처지를 헤아릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This short form shows you understand how hard someone's situation is.

phrases.en: It must have been really bad for him to shout on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 한 행동을 이해해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used to sympathize with something someone did in the past.
phrases.en_equiv: he must have been desperate to...

phrases.en: He must have been truly desperate to borrow money from a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ까요?'로 끝내면 조금 더 부드럽고 혼잣말 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Ending with '-ㄹ까요?' sounds softer, almost like talking to yourself.
phrases.en_equiv: how desperate must they have been

explain_en: It is used in question forms such as '오죽하면 ~겠어요?', '오죽했으면 ~을까요?', and '오죽하겠어요?', showing sympathy: 'it must have been that hard for them.' It expects no answer; you use it to show you understand someone's action or situation.

examples.ko: 그는 자기도취에 빠져 남의 말을 안 들어요.
examples.en: He is lost in self-admiration and doesn't listen to others.
Isn't it self-infatuation to just keep looking in the mirror?
It's hard to work with someone who is extremely self-absorbed.
The lyrics of this song are too self-absorbed.

examples.ko: 자기도취도 적당하면 자신감이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Self-admiration in moderation can become confidence.

examples.ko: 사진을 올릴 때 자기도취일까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I worry that posting photos might look self-obsessed.

explain: 자기 자신이 멋지고 대단하다고 여기며 푹 빠져 있는 모습을 말하고, 대개 부정적으로 써요. '나르시시즘'이라는 외래어도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 '자기도취에 빠졌다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: He got carried away with admiring himself while singing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 모습에 푹 빠져서 주변을 못 본다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests being lost in self-admiration and oblivious to others.

phrases.en: It's hard to talk with someone who is so full of himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정도가 지나친 사람을 비판하듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used somewhat critically about someone who goes too far.

phrases.example: 그 영화에는 나르시시즘이 강한 주인공이 나와요.
phrases.en: That movie has a protagonist with strong narcissism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외래어라서 책이나 영화, 심리 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A loanword more common in talk about books, movies, and psychology.

explain_en: It describes being deeply absorbed in thinking you yourself are wonderful, and it is usually negative. The loanword '나르시시즘' also exists, but in conversation people often say things like '자기도취에 빠졌다'.

examples.ko: 다들 그의 꿈을 조소했지만 그는 포기하지 않았어요.
examples.en: Everyone mocked his dream, but he didn't give up.
He looked at me as if sneering at my mistake.
You shouldn't ridicule other people's failures.
I still remember that scornful look.
There is nothing to gain from ridiculing others.

examples.ko: 그 사람들은 나를 조소하다가 나중에 사과했어요.
examples.en: Those people made fun of me and later apologized.

explain: '비웃다'와 같은 뜻인데 더 글 같은 말이라서 일상 대화에서는 '비웃다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. 반대되는 태도는 '응원하다', '존중하다' 정도예요. 같은 소리의 '조소'가 미술 용어(조각과 소조)로 쓰이기도 하니 문맥을 보고 구분해요.

phrases.en: My friends laughed at my singing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조소하다와 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서는 이 말을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 조소하다 and used far more in daily conversation.

phrases.en: He raised the corners of his mouth as if in mockery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비웃는 것처럼 보이는 모습을 묘사할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to describe something that looks like mockery.

phrases.example: 그는 엉뚱한 계획 때문에 조소를 받았어요.
phrases.en: He was ridiculed because of his odd plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비웃음을 당하는 쪽에서 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used from the point of view of the one being mocked.

explain_en: It means the same as '비웃다' (to laugh at), but is more bookish, so daily conversation uses '비웃다' far more. Opposite attitudes would be '응원하다' or '존중하다'. The same-sounding '조소' is also an art term (sculpture and modeling), so check the context.

t90.ax: I still remember that scornful look.

examples.ko: 그 사람에게 전화할까 골백번도 더 생각했어요.
examples.en: I thought a hundred times about whether to call him.
I've told you countless times, and you still don't listen.
No matter how many times I ask, the answer is the same.

examples.ko: 이 노래를 골백번은 들은 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel like I've listened to this song a million times.

examples.ko: 골백번 고쳐 써도 마음에 안 들어요.
examples.en: No matter how many times I rewrite it, I don't like it.
I resolved countless times to apologize, but I couldn't.

explain: 정확한 숫자가 아니라 '아주 여러 번'이라는 뜻으로 과장해서 하는 말이에요. '골백번도 더'처럼 쓰면 강조가 돼요. 말할 때 자주 쓰고, 격식 있는 글에는 '수없이', '수백 번'이 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: I've heard those words more than a hundred times.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도 더'를 붙이면 정말 많다는 뜻이 훨씬 세져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '도 더' makes the sense of 'far too many times' much stronger.
phrases.en_equiv: more times than I can count

phrases.en: I practiced countless times.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골백번'보다 점잖아서 글이나 격식 있는 말에도 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is more refined than 골백번 and also suits writing and formal speech.

phrases.en: I regretted it a hundred times, wondering why I did that.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후회하다'와 함께 쓰면 깊이 뉘우치는 마음이 강조돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '후회하다', it stresses how deeply you regret something.

explain_en: It is not an exact number but an exaggeration for 'very many times'. Saying '골백번도 더' adds emphasis. It is common in speech, while formal writing suits '수없이' or '수백 번' better.

examples.en: We learned ironic expressions in Korean class.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 반어로 가득해서 읽는 재미가 있어요.
examples.en: This novel is full of irony, which makes it fun to read.

examples.ko: 친구의 칭찬이 반어법이라는 걸 나중에 알았어요.
examples.en: I later realized my friend's compliment was ironic.
You have to hear the tone as well to understand irony.
There was a question about finding irony on the exam.

examples.ko: 그 제목은 반어에 가까워서 처음엔 헷갈렸어요.
examples.en: The title is close to ironic, so I was confused at first.

explain: '반어법'으로 가장 많이 쓰고, 국어 수업이나 문학 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '비꼬다'처럼 말하고, 말투와 표정으로 속뜻을 알 수 있어요. 겉뜻과 속뜻이 반대일 때 '반어', 사실보다 크게 말하는 것은 '과장'이라서 달라요.

phrases.example: 이 시는 반어법을 써서 슬픔을 표현했어요.
phrases.en: This poem expresses sadness by using irony.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반어'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요. 표현 방법 자체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than 반어; it refers to the rhetorical technique itself.

phrases.en: 'Well done' can be an ironic expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉뜻과 속뜻이 반대인 말을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain words whose surface and real meanings are opposite.

phrases.example: 작가가 반어를 써서 주제를 보여 줘요.
phrases.en: The author uses irony to show the theme.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 말에서 반어를 사용하는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the act of employing irony in writing or speech.

explain_en: It is used mostly as '반어법' and comes up in Korean class and talk about literature. In daily life people say things like '비꼬다' (to be sarcastic), and tone and expression reveal the real meaning. '반어' is for when the surface and real meanings are opposite, while '과장' (exaggeration) is saying more than the truth, so they differ.

t90.ax: We learned ironic expressions in Korean class.

examples.ko: 아무러면 싼 옷이 비싼 옷만큼 튼튼하겠어요?
examples.en: Surely a cheap coat can't be as sturdy as an expensive one, right?

examples.ko: 아무러면 처음 하는 사람이 전문가만큼 잘하겠어요?
examples.en: Surely a beginner can't do as well as an expert, can they?
Surely I wouldn't have deceived my friend, would I?
Surely that person wouldn't have lied, would he?

examples.ko: 아무러면 하루 만에 다 배울 수 있겠어요?
examples.en: Surely you can't learn it all in one day, can you?
Surely my parents must understand how I feel, don't they?

explain: 뒤에 '-겠어요?' 같은 반문이 와서 '설마 그럴 리 있겠어요?'라는 뜻을 나타내요. 예스러운 느낌이 있어서 일상 대화에서는 '설마', '아무리 그래도'처럼 말하는 사람도 많아요.

phrases.en: Surely that person wouldn't lie, would he?
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word used more often in everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 아무리 그래도 친구한테 그런 말을 하겠어요?
phrases.en: Even so, would you say that to a friend?
phrases.nuance_ko: '그럴 수 있어도 이건 너무하다'는 느낌으로 반문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to push back, as in 'even if so, this is too much.'

phrases.en: Would I ever tell your secret?
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 쓰는 반말 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form used between close friends.

explain_en: It is followed by a rhetorical question like '-겠어요?' to mean 'How could that possibly be?'. It sounds a bit old-fashioned, so in daily talk many people say '설마' or '아무리 그래도' instead.

t90.ax: Surely that person wouldn't have lied, would he?

en: as if (someone) wouldn't do it well; surely

examples.ko: 걱정하지 마세요, 민수가 어련히 알아서 할까요.
examples.en: Don't worry, Minsu will surely take care of it himself.

examples.ko: 어련히 잘 도착했겠죠. 전화 안 해도 돼요.
examples.en: I'm sure he arrived safely. You don't need to call.
Wouldn't the teacher surely handle the teaching well on their own?
I'm sure they've prepared well. Trust them and wait.
His parents must have decided it properly on their own.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 어련히 잘할까요? 왜 자꾸 확인해요?
examples.en: Of course he'll do it well, won't he? Why do you keep checking?

explain: '어련히 알아서 할까(요)?'처럼 '믿을 만하니 걱정할 필요 없다'는 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. 말투에 따라 '그만 잔소리해요'라는 느낌도 날 수 있어서 윗사람에게는 조심해요.

phrases.en: The child will surely take care of it on their own.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어련히 알아서 할까'의 앞부분으로, 믿으니 걱정 말라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The first part of 'He'll surely handle it', meaning you trust them so there's no need to worry.

phrases.en: I'm sure they'll do well. Just trust them with it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿는다는 뜻이지만 말투에 따라 퉁명스럽게 들릴 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses trust, but can sound a little dismissive depending on tone.

phrases.en: Don't worry. They'll manage fine on their own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어련히와 비슷한 뜻이지만 퉁명스러운 느낌이 없어서 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but without the curt tone, so it's safe to use with superiors.

explain_en: It is used as in '어련히 알아서 할까(요)?' to say that someone can be trusted so there's no need to worry. Depending on tone it can also sound like 'stop nagging', so be careful with people older than you.
